captions.gbp:
Waiting on insurance to approve your scan? That step is called prior authorization: an approval some health plans need before they'll cover a scan. Your doctor's office sends the order and notes, your plan reviews them, and once it's approved the scan is covered under your benefits. If you're using insurance with us, we handle the authorization, verify your benefits and tell you your estimated cost before your visit. Prefer not to wait? Self-pay patients need no referral and no prior authorization: our physician reviews your request the same day, and same-day scans are often available. Self-pay MRI is $295 ($395 with and without contrast), with the radiologist's reading included, and HSA/FSA cards are accepted. While you wait on an approval, ask your plan: did you get my doctor's request, is anything missing, when will you decide, and how do I appeal if it's denied?

Book online at advancedimg.com. General information, not medical advice. Sources: HealthCare.gov; 2025 AMA Prior Authorization Physician Survey.

facts_checked: Prior authorization = approval from a health plan that may be required before you get a service: HealthCare.gov glossary (checked 2026-10-27). 95% of physicians say PA delays access to necessary care; 1,000 practicing physicians: AMA press release on 2025 AMA Prior Authorization Physician Survey, May 13, 2026. Self-pay no referral, same-day physician review, same-day often available; insurance needs a doctor's order and AMI handles authorization/verifies benefits/estimates cost: amiweb no-referral-mri page, insurance page, pricing page, services-data.ts. MRI $295 / $395, radiologist reading included, HSA/FSA: prices.ts, mri-cost-florida page. Checked 2026-10-27.
